items.followUp: Write the chemical reaction of water with chlorine.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the reactants in the reaction.
rubric.how: The answer includes bromine and water.

rubric.why: Award for the correct products of bromine reacting with water.
rubric.how: The answer includes hydrobromic acid and hypobromous acid.

modelAnswer: Br₂ + H₂O ⇌ HBr + HOBr

items.followUp: Write two chemical properties of non-metals.

rubric.why: Metals commonly react with oxygen to form metal oxides.
rubric.how: The answer states that a metal reacts with oxygen to form an oxide.

rubric.why: Metals above hydrogen in the activity series react with dilute acids to release hydrogen gas.
rubric.how: The answer states that a metal reacts with a dilute acid to form a salt and hydrogen.

modelAnswer: Metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
Metals react with dilute acids to form a salt and hydrogen gas: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

items.followUp: State the main postulates of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy definite orbits or shells around the nucleus.
rubric.how: The answer says electrons move around the nucleus in fixed or definite orbits or shells.

rubric.why: Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
rubric.how: The answer states that each orbit or shell has a definite energy.

rubric.why: Electrons do not radiate energy while remaining in a permitted stationary orbit.
rubric.description: No radiation in a stationary orbit
rubric.how: The answer states that electrons do not emit or lose energy while in a permitted orbit.

rubric.why: A change of orbit involves absorption or emission of energy equal to the difference between the two energy levels.
rubric.how: The answer states that electrons absorb or emit energy when they jump between orbits; ΔE = hν is also acceptable.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain fixed circular orbits or shells.
Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
An electron does not radiate energy while it remains in a permitted orbit.
An electron absorbs or emits energy when it moves from one orbit to another; the energy change is ΔE = hν.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an atom and an ion, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: A molecule has no net electrical charge.
rubric.how: The answer identifies a molecule as electrically neutral or having zero net charge.

rubric.why: A molecular ion is a group of bonded atoms carrying a net charge.
rubric.how: The answer identifies a molecular ion as a charged group of atoms.

rubric.why: A molecule consists of two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
rubric.how: The answer describes a molecule as two or more bonded atoms.

rubric.why: A molecular ion forms when a bonded group of atoms gains or loses electrons.
rubric.how: The answer links the ion’s charge to gaining or losing electrons.

rubric.why: A correct example supports the distinction between the two terms.
rubric.how: The answer gives a neutral molecule such as H₂O, O₂ or NH₃.

modelAnswer: A molecule is a neutral group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together, for example H₂O.
A molecular ion is a group of bonded atoms that carries a net electrical charge.
It forms when the group gains or loses one or more electrons.
A molecular ion may be positive, such as NH₄⁺, or negative, such as SO₄²⁻.
Thus, H₂O is a molecule, whereas NH₄⁺ is a molecular ion.

items.followUp: Write five physical properties of non-metals.

rubric.why: A metallic lustre is a characteristic property of metals.
rubric.how: The answer states that metals are lustrous or have a shiny surface.

rubric.why: Metals can generally be hammered into sheets and drawn into wires.
rubric.how: The answer names malleability or ductility; both are included in the model answer.

rubric.why: Metals conduct heat and electricity well.
rubric.how: The answer states that metals are good conductors of heat or electricity.

rubric.why: Sonority, being solid at room temperature, and generally high melting points are other common properties.
rubric.how: The answer names at least one of these properties.

modelAnswer: Metals are generally lustrous (shiny).
They are malleable and can be beaten into sheets.
They are ductile and can be drawn into wires.
They are good conductors of heat and electricity.
They are generally sonorous and solid at room temperature (except mercury).

items.followUp: Define boiling and explain how atmospheric pressure affects the boiling point of a liquid.

rubric.why: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
rubric.how: The answer describes the surface change of a liquid into vapour.

rubric.why: A larger exposed surface lets more liquid particles escape at once.
rubric.how: The answer says increasing surface area increases the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: At higher temperature, more particles have enough energy to escape from the liquid.
rubric.how: The answer says increasing temperature increases the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Humid air already contains more water vapour, so evaporation slows; drier air promotes it.
rubric.how: The answer explains that lower humidity increases evaporation or higher humidity decreases it.

rubric.why: Moving air carries vapour away from the liquid surface and allows further evaporation.
rubric.how: The answer states that stronger air movement or wind increases evaporation.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface, at a temperature below its boiling point.
Surface area: evaporation increases when the exposed surface area increases.
Temperature: higher temperature gives more particles enough energy to escape, so evaporation increases.
Humidity: low humidity increases evaporation; high humidity slows it because the air already contains more water vapour.
Wind speed: stronger wind carries vapour away from the surface and increases evaporation.

items.followUp: Write four differences between a true solution and a colloidal solution.

rubric.why: A colloid is heterogeneous, with a dispersed phase distributed through a dispersion medium.
rubric.how: The answer identifies a colloid as heterogeneous or names its dispersed phase and dispersion medium.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles have sizes approximately between 1 nm and 1000 nm.
rubric.how: The answer gives the colloidal particle-size range as about 1–1000 nm.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles scatter a beam of light, producing the Tyndall effect.
rubric.how: The answer states that colloids scatter light or show the Tyndall effect.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles show continuous random Brownian motion.
rubric.how: The answer identifies the random movement of colloidal particles.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles remain dispersed and do not settle on standing.
rubric.how: The answer states that the particles do not settle on standing or remain suspended.

modelAnswer: A colloid is a heterogeneous mixture in which particles of one substance (the dispersed phase) are distributed through another substance (the dispersion medium).
Colloidal particles are about 1–1000 nm in size.
They scatter light and show the Tyndall effect.
They show continuous random motion called Brownian motion.
They remain dispersed and do not settle on standing.

items.followUp: Define atomic radius and state the approximate atomic radius of a hydrogen atom.

rubric.why: Atomic radius describes the distance from the nucleus to the outermost electron shell.
rubric.how: The answer gives the distance from the nucleus to the outermost shell or energy level.

rubric.why: A numerical example demonstrates the meaning of atomic radius.
rubric.how: The answer gives a suitable atom and approximate radius, such as Na ≈ 186 pm or H ≈ 37 pm.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is the distance from the centre of an atom’s nucleus to its outermost electron shell.
For example, the atomic radius of sodium is about 186 pm.
